description: D'Agostino's skewness test: z from the sample skewness and its p-value from the standard normal; alternative -1 less, 0 two-sided, 1 greater

tolerance.reason: For both outputs, by the rule of ttest_1samp. The skewness b1 = m3 / m2^(3/2) is formed from sums of n rounded terms, so a careful method is off by up to about (kappa_z + n) 2^-53, kappa_z being z's relative condition number in the data (skewtest_rounding_bound); the p-value adds kappa_p = |z phi(z) / P|. The largest bound max(kappa_p, 1) (kappa_z + n) 2^-53 on this grid is 1.6e-12 (n = 100 with an outlier, z = 12.1); 2e-12 is the smallest round value above it (tested). For the exactly symmetric samples every operation in the moments is exact in double arithmetic, so a careful method returns z = 0 exactly (tested). SciPy's worst error is 1.5e-12 except at those symmetric samples, where it returns z = 1.01 to 1.04 instead of 0

grid: samples of n in {8, 10, 20, 50, 100} values: loc + u_i + s u_i^2 with u_i = ((7919 i) mod 1000 - 500) / 1000, loc in {0, 10} and s in {-3, -0.3, 0.01, 0.3, 3}; loc + u_i plus 50 at i = 0 (an outlier); and the exactly symmetric loc + i - (n + 1) / 2, i = 1..n; each with alternative -1 (less), 0 (two-sided) and 1 (greater). |z| from 0 to 12.1, p-value from 4.3e-34 to 1
